title: Round down, then fill the budget

blocks.text: The water utility's analysts keep a fallback for the day the MILP solve is unavailable: round the LP relaxation down, then spend what is left. They want it written once and tested.

Write `round_down_and_fill(shares, projects, budget)` in `fill.py`. `shares` maps each project id to its value $`x_i`$ in the LP relaxation's answer ($`0 \le x_i \le 1`$). The function returns the set of funded ids, built in two steps:

items: **Round down.** Keep every project whose share is 1. A solver returns floating-point numbers, so treat any share greater than $`1 - 10^{-6}`$ as 1.

**Fill.** Walk through all projects in decreasing order of $`\text{value}_i / \text{cost}_i`$, once. Add a project not yet in the plan if all three hold: the plan's cost stays $`\le B`$; its `parent`, if it has one, is already in the plan; and no other project of its `group`, if it has one, is already in the plan.

blocks.text: The result keeps every row of the model in the *Name the rows a rounded plan breaks* practice: the LP's whole projects already did, and each added project is checked. Must-do projects come back at 1 from the LP, so step 1 keeps them. Nothing here proves the plan is the best one.

    return set()

    pipes = [Project("A", 50, 60, must_do=True), Project("B", 40, 52), Project("H", 30, 24), Project("F", 10, 9)]
    print(round_down_and_fill({"A": 1.0, "B": 0.25, "H": 0.0, "F": 0.0}, pipes, 100))

cases.says: the projects the LP funded whole stay, and the money left over buys the projects that still fit
a share of 0.9999999 is a solver's 1, so that project is kept
the fill takes projects in order of value per dollar, not of value
a child whose parent is not in the plan is skipped
a project whose group already has a funded member is skipped
